item.research_question: How does a dual-phase body-centered cubic (BCC) microstructure in an equiatomic AlCrFeNiV high-entropy alloy influence its hardness and wear resistance under dry and lubricated sliding conditions?
item.material_system: Equiatomic AlCrFeNiV high-entropy alloy (Al, Cr, Fe, Ni, V)
item.processing_route: High-energy ball milling (SPEX 8000 mill, 2 h, ball-to-powder ratio 10:1, argon atmosphere) followed by spark plasma sintering (1100 °C for 1 h, 40 MPa axial pressure) and furnace cooling
item.test_conditions: Vickers hardness (5 N load, 15 s hold); reciprocating sliding wear against Al2O3 balls (10 N load, 0.18 m s−1 sliding speed, 30 min duration) under dry and lubricated (deionized water) conditions at ambient temperature
key_findings: Hardness reached 1076 ± 15 HV0.5, significantly higher than previously reported values.
The microstructure consists of two BCC phases: BCC1 (Al, Cr, Fe, Ni) and BCC2 (enriched with 61.9 at.% V and Cr).
Average grain size was measured at 450 nm.
Wear rate under dry conditions was 17.2 × 10−5 mm3 N−1 m−1.
Wear rate under lubricated conditions was 12.4 × 10−5 mm3 N−1 m−1.
Average coefficient of friction (COF) was 0.34 in dry conditions and 0.15 under lubrication.
Hertzian contact stress at 10 N load was calculated to be 1887 MPa.
Oxygen content on the worn surface in dry friction was 2.2 at.% higher than in lubricated friction.
item.mechanism: The superior hardness and wear resistance are attributed to solution strengthening from the mixture of two different BCC systems, high-density grain and phase boundaries acting as barriers to dislocation movement, and the inhibitory effect of the hard BCC2 phase on grain boundary movement and plastic flow. The wear mechanism involves abrasive wear, delamination, and oxidation, where a dense but locally unstable oxide layer forms and fractures, while the tight binding between BCC1 and BCC2 inhibits interfacial crack formation.
item.limitations: The authors note that while hardness is very high, the plasticity of the alloy is poor, making the surface prone to fracture and generating fragments that can cause a secondary grinding effect and increase wear rates.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that the strategy of combining high-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering is beneficial for developing new materials applicable in cutting tools.
quotes: The hardness of the AlCrFeNiV alloys reached 1076 ± 15 HV0.5.
The wear rates of the HEA in dry and lubrication conditions were approximately 17.2 × 10−5 mm3 N−1 m−1 and 12.4 × 10−5 mm3 N−1 m−1, respectively.
The superhigh hardness obtained in the AlCrFeNiV HEA can be attributed to the two different BCC crystal structures formed by the high-energy ball milling combined with a plasma process.
